skill.name: miro-automation
skill.description: Automate Miro boards, items, frames, connectors, and sharing through the Rube MCP integration with current tool schema discovery.
skill.summary: Create, inspect, organize, and share Miro board content through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 54 shell-execution alerts and seven reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown and Miro terminology. The external Rube endpoint is a real trust boundary. State-changing and sharing actions also need explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: Rube MCP and Composio receive delegated Miro access and board data.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose third-party data handling, recommend least-privilege Miro authorization, and tell users how to review or revoke the connection.

remediation.issue: Create, bulk-update, and share workflows lack an immediate confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Show the target board, proposed changes, recipients, and roles before calling any state-changing tool, then require explicit user approval.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Miro connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `miro`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
2. `MIRO_GET_BOARD` - Get detailed info for a specific board [Optional]
- `query`: Search term to filter boards by name
- `board_id`: Specific board ID for detailed retrieval
2. `MIRO_CREATE_STICKY_NOTE_ITEM` - Add sticky notes to a board [Optional]
- `board_id`: Target board ID (required for all item creation)
- `data`: Content object with `content` field for sticky note text
- `style`: Styling object with `fillColor` for sticky note color
- `board_id` is required for ALL item operations; resolve via GET_BOARDS2 first
- Sticky note colors use hex codes (e.g., '#FF0000') in the `fillColor` field
- Frame items require `geometry` with both width and height
1. `MIRO_GET_BOARD_ITEMS` - List all items on a board [Required]
- Results are paginated; follow `cursor` until absent for complete item list
- `emails`: Array of email addresses to invite
- `startItem`: Object with `id` of the source item
- `endItem`: Object with `id` of the target item
- Use `position: {x: 0, y: 0}` for center of board
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Email addresses must be valid; invalid emails cause the entire request to fail
1. Call MIRO_GET_BOARD_ITEMS with board_id and optional type filter
3. Extract item id for further operations

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party MCP Handles Delegated Miro Access
semantic_findings.description: Miro authentication and operations pass through Rube MCP and Composio, exposing delegated account access and board data to an additional service provider.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly names Composio, directs installation of the Rube MCP endpoint, and requires Miro OAuth through the returned authentication link.

semantic_findings.title: No Explicit Confirmation for External Side Effects
semantic_findings.description: Board creation, bulk content changes, and access grants can alter a workspace, but the workflows do not require confirmation immediately before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflows invoke create and share tools with user-selected targets, yet neither section includes a preview or final approval requirement.

content.value_statement: Manual board setup and maintenance consume collaboration time. This skill uses Rube MCP to find, create, organize, connect, and share Miro content.
actual_capabilities: Searches current Rube MCP tool schemas before selecting Miro operations.
Lists Miro boards and resolves board names to board identifiers.
Creates boards, sticky notes, frames, and multiple items in bulk.
Lists board items and connectors with the required pagination method.
Shares boards with specified email addresses and access roles.
Uses positions, dimensions, colors, and item identifiers to organize board content.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP, a Miro OAuth connection, and sufficient Miro workspace permissions.
Available operations and parameters depend on the current Rube MCP tool schemas.
Miro rate limits, item limits, and organization policies can restrict workflows.
The documented workflows do not provide transaction rollback for completed changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Workshop Board
use_cases.description: Create frames and color-coded sticky notes for workshop topics, then place them in a clear board layout.

use_cases.title: Map Product Work
use_cases.description: Find an existing planning board, add grouped work items, and connect related items for review.

use_cases.title: Manage Board Access
use_cases.description: Locate a board, review its members, and prepare invitations with defined viewer, commenter, or editor roles.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Miro boards matching [name]. List the closest matches with modification details, and do not change any board.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workshop Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Miro board named [name] with frames for [sections]. Preview the layout and sticky note text before creating anything.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Existing Items
prompt_templates.prompt: On board [name], find [item types], group them by [rule], and propose positions and connectors. Ask for approval before applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Share a Planning Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a planning board from [content], use bulk creation where supported, validate pagination, then preview recipients and roles before sharing.

output_examples.input: Find the quarterly planning board and summarize its sticky notes and connectors.
output_examples.output: Found one matching board. It contains 38 sticky notes across four frames and 12 connectors. No board content was changed.

output_examples.input: Prepare a retrospective board with three sections and invite two reviewers.
output_examples.output: Prepared a preview with three frames and nine starter notes. Sharing remains pending until you confirm both reviewer addresses and their roles.

output_examples.input: Add 60 backlog notes to the product board and group them by theme.
output_examples.output: Resolved the target board and grouped 60 notes into five themes. The proposed bulk changes are ready for confirmation.

best_practices: Resolve board names to identifiers and confirm the selected board before making changes.
Search current tool schemas and validate required fields before every workflow.
Preview content, recipients, and access roles before any create or share operation.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode board or item identifiers across Miro accounts.
Do not invite users or assign editor access without explicit approval.
Do not ignore pagination when listing boards, items, members, or connectors.

faq.question: What accounts and connections are required?
faq.answer: You need Rube MCP, an active Miro OAuth connection, and permissions for each requested board operation.

faq.question: Can this skill create complete Miro boards?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create boards, frames, sticky notes, positioned items, and bulk item sets when the current tools support them.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing board?
faq.answer: Yes. It can find boards, list their items, inspect connectors, and prepare supported changes.

faq.question: How does the skill handle large boards?
faq.answer: It follows offset pagination for board lists and cursor pagination for board items. Type filters can reduce large result sets.

faq.question: Can it share boards with other people?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare invitations for valid email addresses with viewer, commenter, or editor roles, subject to workspace policies.

faq.question: Does the skill send data to another service?
faq.answer: Yes. Rube MCP and Composio broker Miro authentication and operations, so their data handling and authorization policies apply.
